branches.en: The engineer and the engineering are one idea.
branches.cn: 工程师与工程设计是同一概念。

branches.en: Building and plotting both require a plan.
branches.cn: 建造与策划都需要计划。

intro.en: Engineer is engine plus -eer, the old ending for a person's trade.
intro.cn: engineer 是 engine 加 -eer，即表示职业者的古老词尾。

latinIntro.en: The family traces to Latin ingenium, talent, through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族经法语追溯到拉丁语 ingenium（天赋）。

items.example: Engine is the base of engineer.
items.exampleCN: engine 是 engineer 的基础。

items.meaning: to plan how something will be made

definition_en: to improve the quality, strength, or value of something
core_image: 把一件东西一点点垫高，让它在光线下显得更亮、更有分量
scene: 新来的教练没有换掉旧战术，只是把训练强度一点点提上去，球队的速度明显变快。The new coach enhanced the team's speed with small daily drills.
sceneCN: 这里 enhance 是「提高；增强」（第 1 个义项：改善质量或水平）；句意：新教练通过每天的小训练提高了球队的速度。

senses.title: To improve quality
senses.definition: to make something better in quality, usefulness, or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在质量、实用性或外观上变得更好
senses.example: The new windows enhance the look of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 新窗户提升了房子的外观。
senses.why: The word comes from a root meaning high, so enhancing is lifting something to a higher standard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「高」的词根，所以 enhance 就是把某物提升到更高的水准。

senses.title: To increase strength or degree
senses.definition: to increase the strength, effect, or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 增加某物的强度、效果或数量
senses.example: Regular exercise enhances the body's ability to resist illness.
senses.exampleCN: 规律运动增强身体抵抗疾病的能力。
senses.why: Lifting something higher also means raising its intensity, which gives the sense of strengthening.
senses.whyCN: 把某物抬得更高也意味着提高其强度，于是产生「加强」这一义项。

senses.title: To raise value
senses.definition: to increase the money or social value of something
senses.definitionCN: 提高某物的金钱价值或社会价值
senses.example: The restoration enhanced the value of the old building.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修复提升了这栋老建筑的价值。
senses.why: If quality rises, the price or worth people assign to it can rise too.
senses.whyCN: 如果质量提高，人们赋予它的价格或价值也会随之上升。

intro.en: Enhance comes through Old French enhaucier from Vulgar Latin altiare, to raise, from Latin altus, high.
intro.cn: enhance 经古法语 enhaucier 来自俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高），其根源是拉丁语 altus（高的）。

items.en: Altus means high or deep, and it also gives English altitude.
items.cn: altus 意为高的或深的，也是英语 altitude 的来源。

items.en: Altiare means to make high or raise up.
items.cn: altiare 意为使变高、抬高。

items.en: Old French enhaucier adds en- and means to raise or exalt.
items.cn: 古法语 enhaucier 加上 en-，意为抬高或提升。

items.en: The French verb crosses into English law and courtly writing.
items.cn: 这个法语动词进入英语的法律与宫廷写作。

items.en: Middle English enhance means to raise in rank, value, or dignity.
items.cn: 中古英语 enhance 指提高等级、价值或尊严。

items.en: Modern English widens the word to quality, performance, and effect.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到质量、表现和效果。

note.en: Enhance belongs to a family about making something better or higher, and it sits near words for improving and increasing.
note.cn: enhance 属于「使某物更好或更高」的词族，与改善和增加类词相邻。

entries.definition: something that improves or strengthens an effect
to make a feeling or effect stronger

normalIntro.en: Enhance sounds like in hance, and the image is lifting something higher, which matches its Latin root for high.
normalIntro.cn: enhance 读起来像 in hance，画面是把东西往高处抬，这正对应它表示「高」的拉丁词根。

normal.en: The en- at the front means make or put into, so enhance is to put something into a higher state.
normal.cn: 开头的 en- 表示「使、置入」，所以 enhance 就是使某物进入更高的状态。

normal.en: Enhance the quality is the most common pattern in modern writing.
normal.cn: enhance the quality 是现代写作中最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Enhance and improvement belong together: the verb and the noun.
normal.cn: enhance 与 improvement 相配：一个是动词，一个是名词。

normal.en: The ending -ment in enhancement turns the action into a noun.
normal.cn: enhancement 中的 -ment 把动作变成名词。

normal.en: Compare increase: increase is about amount, enhance is about quality or value.
normal.cn: 对比 increase：increase 侧重数量，enhance 侧重质量或价值。

abstract.en: Picture a painting lit from below so its colours seem richer.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画从下方打光，颜色显得更饱满。

abstract.en: Imagine a sound system turned up just enough to fill the room.
abstract.cn: 想象音响被调到刚好填满房间的程度。

abstract.en: Think of a rough stone polished until its pattern shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一块粗石被磨亮，纹理显现出来。

examples.en: Good lighting can enhance the colours in a photograph.
examples.cn: 好的光线能增强照片里的色彩。

examples.en: The course is designed to enhance students' writing skills.
examples.cn: 这门课程旨在提高学生的写作能力。

examples.en: A famous tenant enhanced the reputation of the building.
examples.cn: 一位有名气的租户提升了这栋楼的声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩汉斯」——恩惠把水平往上抬，就是提高；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 altus（高的）→ 俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高）→ 古法语 enhaucier → 中古英语 enhance，本义「抬高、提升」，后指提高质量与价值。

sensesIntro.en: Lifting something higher gives three results: better quality, greater strength, and higher value.
sensesIntro.cn: 把某物抬得更高带来三种结果：质量更好、强度更大、价值更高。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something lifted to a higher level so that it shows better.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被抬到更高的层次，因而显得更好。

branches.en: Improving quality is the most general modern sense.
branches.cn: 提高质量，是最概括的现代义项。

branches.en: Raising intensity gives the sense of strengthening.
branches.cn: 提高强度，产生「加强」这一义项。

branches.en: Raising worth gives the sense of increasing value.
branches.cn: 提高价值，产生「增值」这一义项。

branches.en: Better quality and higher value usually rise together.
branches.cn: 质量更好与价值更高通常一起上升。

branches.en: Strength and value both measure the higher level the thing has reached.
branches.cn: 强度与价值都衡量事物所达到的更高水平。

intro.en: Enhance is a French-shaped verb built on a Latin root for high, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: enhance 是法语形态的动词，建立在表示「高」的拉丁词根上，其词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin altus means high, and altiare means to raise, which becomes enhaucier in French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 altus 表示高，altiare 表示抬高，在法语中变成 enhaucier。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 enhance 与 enlarge 开头。

items.example: Altus is the root behind enhance.
items.exampleCN: altus 是 enhance 背后的词根。

items.example: Altiare carries the idea of lifting.
Enhaucier brings the word into English.
items.exampleCN: enhaucier 把这个词带入英语。
enhance 保留了「抬高」的画面。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

definition_en: to get pleasure from something, or to have the use or benefit of something good
core_image: 坐在阳光下的长椅上，慢慢咬一口甜点，眼睛不自觉地弯起来
scene: 演出结束后，观众还坐在座位上不愿走，脸上都是笑。Everyone seemed to enjoy the music more than the food.
sceneCN: 这里 enjoy 是「享受；喜爱」（第 1 个义项：从某事物中获得快乐）；句意：大家似乎更享受音乐而不是食物。

senses.title: To take pleasure in something
senses.definition: to get pleasure or satisfaction from an activity or experience
senses.definitionCN: 从某项活动或经历中获得快乐或满足
senses.example: She enjoys walking by the river after work.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢下班后沿河散步。
senses.why: The Old French verb means to rejoice, so the core sense is the pleasure taken in something.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词意为「欢欣」，所以核心义是从某事物中获得的快乐。

senses.title: To have the benefit of something
senses.definition: to have the use or advantage of something good
senses.definitionCN: 拥有并使用某种有利条件
senses.example: The town enjoys clean air and quiet streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇享有清新的空气和安静的街道。
senses.why: If something gives you pleasure, you are in a position to use it, which leads to the sense of possessing a benefit.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物带给你快乐，你就处于可以使用它的位置，于是引申出「享有」某种好处。

senses.title: To have a good time
senses.definition: to feel happy and amused in a situation, especially with others
senses.definitionCN: 在某种场合中尤其与他人一起感到愉快
senses.example: The children enjoyed themselves at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在聚会上玩得很开心。
senses.why: The reflexive form enjoy oneself makes the person the source and target of the pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式 enjoy oneself 让人既是快乐的来源，也是承受者。

intro.en: Enjoy comes through Old French enjoir, to rejoice, from Latin gaudere, to be glad.
intro.cn: enjoy 经古法语 enjoir（欢欣）来自拉丁语 gaudere（高兴）。

items.en: Gaudere means to be glad or rejoice, and it also gives English joy.
items.cn: gaudere 意为高兴或欢欣，也是英语 joy 的来源。

items.en: Enjoir adds en- to joir and means to take pleasure in something.
items.cn: enjoir 在 joir 前加 en-，意为从某物中获得快乐。

items.en: The verb enters English law and daily speech with the sense of possessing a right.
items.cn: 这个动词进入英语的法律与日常用语，带有「享有权利」的意思。

items.en: Middle English enjoy covers both pleasure and the possession of benefits.
items.cn: 中古英语 enjoy 既指快乐，也指享有好处。

items.en: Enjoy oneself becomes a fixed phrase for having a good time.
items.cn: enjoy oneself 成为表示玩得开心的固定短语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the pleasure sense as the dominant one.
items.cn: 现代英语以「享受、喜爱」为主要义项。

note.en: Enjoy belongs to the joy family, and it sits near verbs for liking, savouring, and appreciating.
note.cn: enjoy 属于 joy 词族，与喜欢、品味和欣赏类动词相邻。

entries.definition: to enjoy a taste or experience slowly
to recognize and enjoy the value of something

normalIntro.en: Enjoy contains joy, so the spelling itself gives the memory hook: to enjoy is to put joy into what you are doing.
normalIntro.cn: enjoy 含有 joy，拼写本身就给出记忆钩子：enjoy 就是把快乐放进正在做的事里。

normal.en: See joy inside enjoy: the word is joy with en- in front.
normal.cn: 在 enjoy 里看到 joy：这个词就是前面加 en- 的 joy。

normal.en: Enjoy doing is the pattern when the activity itself is the pleasure.
normal.cn: enjoy doing 是「活动本身带来快乐」的句型。

normal.en: Enjoy oneself means put yourself into a joyful state.
normal.cn: enjoy oneself 意为让自己进入快乐的状态。

normal.en: Enjoy good health is the possessive sense: you have health and benefit from it.
normal.cn: enjoy good health 是「享有」义：拥有健康并从中受益。

normal.en: Compare enjoyable: the adjective describes something that gives joy.
normal.cn: 对比 enjoyable：形容词描述「带来快乐的东西」。

abstract.en: Picture a child running through a sprinkler with a wide open smile.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子在喷水器下奔跑，笑得合不拢嘴。

abstract.en: Imagine a cup of tea held in both hands on a cold morning.
abstract.cn: 想象寒冷早晨双手捧着一杯茶。

abstract.en: Think of a song you replay because the first note lifts you.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌，第一个音就让你心情上扬，于是反复播放。

examples.en: I really enjoyed the concert last night.
examples.cn: 我昨晚非常享受那场音乐会。

examples.en: The village enjoys a mild climate all year.
examples.cn: 这个村庄全年气候温和。

examples.en: Make sure the guests enjoy themselves.
examples.cn: 一定要让客人们玩得开心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因久爱」——因为长久喜爱，所以享受其中；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gaudere（高兴）→ 古法语 joir（欢欣）→ enjoir（从……获得快乐）→ 中古英语 enjoy，兼指享受与享有。

sensesIntro.en: Pleasure comes first, then the possession of something that gives pleasure, then the reflexive phrase for having a good time.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是从中获得快乐，再是拥有带来快乐的东西，最后是表示玩得开心的反身短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: joy taken into oneself from something being done or possessed.
core.cn: 核心意象：从正在做或拥有的事物中，把快乐收进自己心里。

branches.en: Taking pleasure in an activity is the core sense.
branches.cn: 从活动中获得快乐，是核心义项。

branches.en: Having a benefit and using it is the possessive sense.
branches.cn: 拥有并使用某种好处，是「享有」义项。

branches.en: The reflexive form describes a person filled with pleasure.
branches.cn: 反身形式描述一个人充满快乐。

branches.en: What gives pleasure and what one possesses can be the same good thing.
branches.cn: 带来快乐的东西与所拥有的好处可以是同一样东西。

branches.en: Enjoying a benefit and enjoying oneself both describe wellbeing.
branches.cn: 享有好处与玩得开心都描述一种良好状态。

intro.en: Enjoy is a French-shaped verb whose family grows with English adjective and noun endings.
intro.cn: enjoy 是法语形态的动词，其词族由英语形容词和名词词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin gaudere means to rejoice, and its French descendant joir gives the joy inside enjoy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gaudere 意为欢欣，其法语后裔 joir 提供了 enjoy 中的 joy。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 enjoy 与 enliven 开头。

items.example: Gaudere is the root of joy and enjoy.
items.exampleCN: gaudere 是 joy 与 enjoy 的词根。

items.example: Joir supplies the joy element in enjoy.
items.exampleCN: joir 提供 enjoy 中的 joy 成分。

items.example: Enjoir brings the verb into English.
items.exampleCN: enjoir 把这个动词带入英语。

items.example: Enjoy keeps the French verb shape.
items.exampleCN: enjoy 保留了法语动词形态。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

definition_en: giving pleasure and making you feel happy
core_image: 一场让人从头笑到尾的聚会，散场时大家还在门口聊天
scene: 周末的午后，一群孩子在草地上追着风筝跑，笑声不断。It was an enjoyable afternoon for everyone in the park.
sceneCN: 这里 enjoyable 是「令人愉快的」（第 1 个义项：能带来快乐的）；句意：对公园里的每个人来说，这都是一个愉快的下午。

senses.title: Giving pleasure
senses.definition: making you feel happy and interested
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到快乐并投入其中
senses.example: It was an enjoyable evening with old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个和老朋友共度的愉快夜晚。
senses.why: The -able ending means able to give, so enjoyable describes something that gives enjoyment.
senses.whyCN: -able 词尾表示「能够给予」，所以 enjoyable 描述「能带来享受的事物」。

senses.title: Pleasant rather than exciting
senses.definition: pleasant and easy to like, without being very intense
senses.definitionCN: 令人舒服、容易喜欢，但不算特别激烈
senses.example: The book is enjoyable but not very deep.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书读起来轻松愉快，但不算深刻。
senses.why: Enjoyment can be quiet as well as intense, so the adjective covers mild pleasantness too.
senses.whyCN: 享受可以安静也可以强烈，所以这个形容词也涵盖温和的愉悦。

intro.en: Enjoyable is enjoy plus the ending -able, meaning able to give enjoyment.
intro.cn: enjoyable 是 enjoy 加词尾 -able，意为「能够带来享受的」。

items.en: Gaudere means to rejoice and lies behind the joy in enjoy.
items.cn: gaudere 意为欢欣，是 enjoy 中 joy 的来源。

items.en: Enjoir means to take pleasure in something.
items.cn: enjoir 意为从某物中获得快乐。

items.en: Middle English enjoy names the act of taking pleasure.
items.cn: 中古英语 enjoy 指获得快乐的动作。

items.en: English adds -able to form enjoyable, able to give pleasure.
items.cn: 英语加 -able 构成 enjoyable，意为「能带来快乐的」。

items.en: The word spreads in reviews and travel writing as a mild praise.
items.cn: 这个词在评论和游记中传播，用作温和的赞美。

items.en: Modern English uses it for experiences that are pleasant and satisfying.
items.cn: 现代英语用它描述愉快而令人满足的经历。

note.en: Enjoyable is the adjective of enjoy, and it sits near pleasant and entertaining words without their stronger claims.
note.cn: enjoyable 是 enjoy 的形容词，与 pleasant、entertaining 等词相邻，但语气更温和。

entries.definition: giving a mild feeling of pleasure
interesting and amusing to watch or read

normalIntro.en: Enjoyable is just enjoy plus -able, so anything that can be enjoyed is enjoyable.
normalIntro.cn: enjoyable 就是 enjoy 加 -able，所以任何能被享受的东西都是 enjoyable。

normal.en: Take enjoy, add -able: able to give joy.
normal.cn: 取 enjoy 加 -able：能够带来快乐。

normal.en: An enjoyable experience is one you would gladly repeat.
normal.cn: an enjoyable experience 是一段你愿意再经历一次的经历。

normal.en: The ending -ably turns it into the adverb enjoyably.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ably 把它变成副词 enjoyably。

normal.en: Compare enjoyable and delighted: one gives pleasure, one feels it.
normal.cn: 对比 enjoyable 与 delighted：一个给予快乐，一个感受快乐。

normal.en: Highly enjoyable is a common way to praise a book or show.
normal.cn: highly enjoyable 是赞美书或演出的常用说法。

abstract.en: Picture a picnic where nobody wants to pack up.
abstract.cn: 想象一次野餐，谁也不想收拾离开。

abstract.en: Imagine a film that makes the whole row laugh at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一部让整排观众同时发笑的电影。

abstract.en: Think of a walk with no destination but good company.
abstract.cn: 想象一次没有目的地、只有好同伴的散步。

examples.en: We had an enjoyable afternoon by the lake.
examples.cn: 我们在湖边度过了一个愉快的下午。

examples.en: The class is both enjoyable and useful.
examples.cn: 这门课既有趣又有用。

examples.en: She found the work surprisingly enjoyable.
examples.cn: 她发现这份工作出乎意料地令人愉快。

dict_mnemonic.text: enjoy（享受）+ -able（能……的）＝能带来享受的，即令人愉快的；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: enjoy（享受，源自拉丁语 gaudere「欢欣」）+ 形容词词尾 -able，表示「能够带来快乐的」。

sensesIntro.en: Something that gives pleasure is the basic sense, and milder pleasantness is its quieter extension.
sensesIntro.cn: 能带来快乐是基本义，而较温和的愉悦是它更安静的延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an experience people would happily repeat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段人们愿意再来一次的经历。

branches.en: Giving pleasure is the direct meaning of the -able form.
branches.cn: 带来快乐，是 -able 形式的直接含义。

branches.en: Mild pleasantness is a quieter degree of the same pleasure.
branches.cn: 温和的愉悦，是同样快乐中更轻的程度。

branches.en: Both strong fun and quiet comfort count as enjoyable.
branches.cn: 热闹的乐趣与安静的舒适都算 enjoyable。

branches.en: The adjective describes the experience, not the person feeling it.
branches.cn: 这个形容词描述经历本身，而不是感受它的人。

branches.en: It often appears as modest praise rather than high excitement.
branches.cn: 它常作为温和赞美出现，而不是高度兴奋。

intro.en: Enjoyable is a transparent English adjective: enjoy plus -able.
intro.cn: enjoyable 是构词透明的英语形容词：enjoy 加 -able。

latinIntro.en: The base enjoy goes back to Latin gaudere, to rejoice, and -able means able to give.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 enjoy 可上溯到拉丁语 gaudere（欢欣），-able 表示「能够给予」。

items.example: Enjoy is the base of enjoyable.
items.exampleCN: enjoy 是 enjoyable 的基础词。
enjoyable 由 enjoy 与 -able 合成。
enjoyment 共享 enjoy 词干。

items.example: Gaudere is the distant root of enjoy.
items.exampleCN: gaudere 是 enjoy 的远源。

items.example: En- opens the base verb enjoy.
items.exampleCN: en- 出现在基础动词 enjoy 开头。

definition_en: extremely large in size, amount, or degree
core_image: 一头鲸从船边浮起，船在它旁边像一片叶子
scene: 博物馆大厅中央立着一具恐龙骨架，参观者站在下面显得很小。The skeleton was enormous, filling the whole hall.
sceneCN: 这里 enormous 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项：尺寸极大）；句意：这具骨架极其巨大，占满了整个大厅。

senses.title: Extremely large in size
senses.definition: much bigger than usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 比通常或预期大得多
senses.example: An enormous tree stood in the middle of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 花园中央立着一棵巨大的树。
senses.why: The Latin source means outside the rule, and something outside normal measure is first of all huge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「超出常规」，而超出常规尺度的东西首先就是巨大的。

senses.title: Extremely great in degree
senses.definition: very great in amount, power, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、力量或重要性上极大
senses.example: The project required an enormous amount of work.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目需要极大的工作量。
senses.why: The same sense of exceeding normal limits applies to abstract quantities such as effort and pressure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「超出正常限度」也适用于努力、压力等抽象数量。

senses.title: Outrageous or monstrous
senses.definition: shockingly bad or wicked, an older literary sense
senses.definitionCN: 令人震惊地坏或邪恶，较古老的文学义项
senses.example: The poem describes an enormous crime against the innocent.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗描述了一桩针对无辜者的骇人罪行。
senses.why: Something outside the rule of right conduct was originally called enormous before the word shifted to size.
senses.whyCN: 超出正当行为之「常规」的事，原本就被称作 enormous，后来词义才转向尺寸。

intro.en: Enormous comes from Latin enormis, outside the rule, from e-, out of, and norma, a rule or square.
intro.cn: enormous 来自拉丁语 enormis（超出常规），由 e-（出于）与 norma（规则、曲尺）构成。

items.en: Norma means a carpenter's square and then any rule or standard.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的曲尺，后来泛指规则或标准。

items.en: Enormis means out of rule, irregular, and therefore monstrous or shocking.
items.cn: enormis 意为不合规则的、异常的，因此有「骇人」之意。

items.en: Old French enorme keeps the sense of something shocking and excessive.
items.cn: 古法语 enorme 保留「骇人、过度」的意思。

items.en: Middle English enormous describes both wicked acts and great size.
items.cn: 中古英语 enormous 既描述邪恶行为，也描述巨大尺寸。

items.en: The size sense becomes dominant in ordinary usage.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，尺寸义在日常用法中占据主导。

items.en: Modern English uses enormous mainly for very great size or amount.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 enormous 表示极大的尺寸或数量。

note.en: Enormous belongs to the norm family, and it sits near adjectives for very great size.
note.cn: enormous 属于「常规」词族，与表示极大尺寸的形容词相邻。

entries.definition: the great size or seriousness of something
extremely wide or great in area

normalIntro.en: Enormous contains norm, so the memory hook is something so big that it is outside the normal measure.
normalIntro.cn: enormous 含有 norm，记忆钩子是「大到超出了正常尺度」。

normal.en: E- means out of, and norm means rule: outside the rule, therefore huge.
normal.cn: e- 表示出于，norm 表示规则：超出规则，所以巨大。

normal.en: Enormous amount is the most common abstract collocation.
normal.cn: enormous amount 是最常见的抽象搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ly gives enormously, meaning very much.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 构成 enormously，意为「极大地」。

normal.en: Compare huge and enormous: enormous often adds a sense of excess.
normal.cn: 对比 huge 与 enormous：enormous 常多一层「过度」的意味。

normal.en: The noun enormity can mean great seriousness as well as great size.
normal.cn: 名词 enormity 既可指巨大，也可指严重性。

abstract.en: Picture a whale surfacing beside a small boat.
abstract.cn: 想象一头鲸在小船旁浮出水面。

abstract.en: Imagine standing under a dinosaur skeleton that fills a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象站在占满大厅的恐龙骨架下面。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow so long it reaches across a whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象一道影子长到横跨整条街。

examples.en: The stadium was filled with an enormous crowd.
examples.cn: 体育场里挤满了庞大的人群。

examples.en: She felt enormous relief when the test was over.
examples.cn: 考试结束后她感到极大的宽慰。

examples.en: Building the bridge took an enormous effort.
examples.cn: 修建这座桥付出了巨大的努力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一挪磨死」——一块石头要挪动会磨死人，因为它实在太大了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 e-（出于）+ norma（规则、曲尺）→ enormis（不合常规的、骇人的）→ 古法语 enorme → 中古英语 enormous，后以「巨大」为主要义项。

sensesIntro.en: Being outside the rule first described monstrous things, then huge ones, and the size sense now reaches both physical and abstract quantities.
sensesIntro.cn: 「超出常规」最初描述骇人之物，随后转向巨大之物，如今尺寸义既覆盖具体物体也覆盖抽象数量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something so large that it exceeds every normal measure.
core.cn: 核心意象：某个东西大到超越一切正常尺度。

branches.en: Physical size beyond expectation is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 超出预期的物理尺寸，是日常义项。

branches.en: Abstract quantity beyond expectation extends the same excess.
branches.cn: 超出预期的抽象数量，延伸同样的「过度」。

branches.en: The old sense of monstrous or outrageous keeps the moral origin alive.
branches.cn: 「骇人、极恶」的旧义保留了这个词的道德起源。

branches.en: Big objects and big amounts both break the normal scale.
branches.cn: 巨大物体与巨大数量都突破正常尺度。

branches.en: Excess in degree can impress or horrify, depending on context.
branches.cn: 程度上的过度既可令人惊叹，也可令人惊骇。

intro.en: Enormous is a Latin adjective built from a prefix and the noun norma, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: enormous 是由前缀与名词 norma 构成的拉丁形容词，其词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The prefix e- means out of, and norma means rule, so enormis is outside the rule.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 e- 表示出于，norma 表示规则，所以 enormis 就是「超出规则」。

items.exampleCN: e- 出现在 enormis 与 enormous 开头。

items.example: Norma is the root of enormous and norm.
items.exampleCN: norma 是 enormous 与 norm 的词根。
enormis 由 e- 与 norma 合成。

items.example: Enormous keeps the idea of exceeding measure.
items.exampleCN: enormous 保留了「超出尺度」的意思。

items.example: Enormity adds -ity to the same stem.

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词词尾

definition_en: as much or as many as is needed, or to the degree that is needed
core_image: 碗里的饭刚好吃到饱，不多不少
scene: 锅里还剩半锅汤，主人看了看人数，说这些已经够了。There is enough soup for everyone at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 enough 是「足够的」（第 1 个义项：数量满足需要）；句意：这锅汤足够桌上每个人喝。

derivatives.zh: 足够的（古语或方言变体）

senses.title: As much as is needed
senses.definition: the amount or number that is necessary, and no more
senses.definitionCN: 达到必要程度、不必再多的数量
senses.example: Do we have enough chairs for the guests?
senses.exampleCN: 我们有足够的椅子给客人吗？
senses.why: The Old English word means sufficient, so the core sense is the exact amount a need requires.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词义为「充足的」，所以核心义正是满足需要所需的那个量。

senses.title: To the necessary degree
senses.definition: to the degree that is necessary, used before an adjective or adverb
senses.definitionCN: 达到必要程度，用于形容词或副词之前
senses.example: The water is warm enough for swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 水温已经足够暖和，可以游泳了。
senses.why: The same measure of sufficiency applies to qualities, not only to countable things.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「充足尺度」也适用于性质，而不只是可数事物。

senses.title: Stop, that is too much
senses.definition: used to tell someone that something has gone far enough
senses.definitionCN: 用于告诉某人某事已经过头，应当停止
senses.example: Enough! We have heard the same excuse all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 够了！这个借口我们听了一上午了。
senses.why: When the needed amount is reached, anything further is excess, which gives the word its boundary-setting use.
senses.whyCN: 当所需之量已经达到，再多就是多余，于是这个词有了「划定界限」的用法。

intro.en: Enough comes from Old English genōh, a Germanic word related to German genug.
intro.cn: enough 来自古英语 genōh，是一个与德语 genug 同源的日耳曼词。

items.en: Genōh means sufficient, and it already works as adjective and adverb.
items.cn: genōh 意为充足的，已经兼作形容词和副词。

items.en: The prefix ge- adds a sense of completeness to the root.
items.cn: 前缀 ge- 给词根增添「完成、完备」的意味。

items.en: Middle English ynough simplifies the spelling and keeps the meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语 ynough 简化拼写，保留词义。

items.en: Enough settles into its modern spelling and fixed phrases.
items.cn: enough 固定为现代拼写，并进入固定短语。

items.en: Enough works as adjective, adverb, pronoun, and interjection.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enough 可作形容词、副词、代词和感叹词。

items.en: The word now also appears in idioms such as strangely enough.
items.cn: 如今这个词还出现在 strangely enough 等习语中。

note.en: Enough shares the -ough spelling with several unrelated words, and its meaning sits with sufficient and adequate.
note.cn: enough 与几个不相干的词共享 -ough 拼写，词义则与 sufficient、adequate 相邻。

entries.definition: a large amount, more than enough

normalIntro.en: Enough is a short Germanic word, so the hooks use its sound and its common phrases rather than Latin roots.
normalIntro.cn: enough 是一个简短的日耳曼词，所以记忆钩子用读音和常见短语，而不是拉丁词根。

normal.en: Enough sounds like ee-nuff, and nuff is close to the sound of a full stomach saying stop.
normal.cn: enough 读作 ee-nuff，nuff 听起来像吃饱后说「够了」。

normal.en: Good enough is the phrase for something that meets the need without being perfect.
normal.cn: good enough 指满足需要、不必完美。

normal.en: Enough time is the most common adjective use.
normal.cn: enough time 是最常见的形容词用法。

normal.en: More than enough means there is extra.
normal.cn: more than enough 意为还有富余。

normal.en: Strangely enough is a fixed phrase meaning surprisingly.
normal.cn: strangely enough 是固定短语，意为「说来奇怪」。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl filled exactly to the line you wanted.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗刚好盛到你想要的那条线。

abstract.en: Imagine a host counting seats and finding one left over.
abstract.cn: 想象主人数座位，发现还剩一个。

abstract.en: Think of a hand raised to stop a second helping.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起，拦住再来一份。

examples.en: We have enough food for the whole week.
examples.cn: 我们的食物够吃一整周。

examples.en: The room was warm enough to sit in.
examples.cn: 房间足够暖和，可以坐人。

examples.en: Enough! Let us start the meeting.
examples.cn: 够了！我们开始开会吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一拿夫」——一拿起来就觉得分量刚好，够用；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 genōh（充足的），属日耳曼语族，与德语 genug 同源；前缀 ge- 表完备，后拼写演变为 enough。

sensesIntro.en: The exact needed amount comes first, then the needed degree, and finally the boundary where anything more is too much.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是恰好满足需要的量，再是必要的程度，最后是「再多就过头」的界限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measure filled exactly to the needed line.
core.cn: 核心意象：分量刚好填到需要的那条线。

branches.en: Sufficient quantity is the core adjective sense.
branches.cn: 足够的数量，是核心形容词义项。

branches.en: Sufficient degree applies the same measure to qualities.
branches.cn: 足够的程度，把同一尺度用于性质。

branches.en: Reaching the line makes further amounts excessive, hence stop.
branches.cn: 达到那条线后，再多就是过剩，于是表示「停止」。

branches.en: Enough things and enough warmth both meet a required level.
branches.cn: 足够的物品与足够的温度都达到所需水平。

branches.en: The point of sufficiency is also the point to stop.
branches.cn: 「足够」的那一刻，也是该停下的那一刻。

intro.en: Enough is a Germanic word, so its parts are Old English rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: enough 是日耳曼词，其成分是古英语而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in enough; the word descends from Old English genōh.
latinIntro.cn: enough 没有拉丁成分，这个词源自日耳曼语，继承了古英语 genōh。

items.example: Ge- appears in the old form genōh.
items.exampleCN: ge- 出现在古形式 genōh 中。

items.example: Genōh is the ancestor of enough.
items.exampleCN: genōh 是 enough 的祖先。

items.example: Ynough is the Middle English spelling.
Enough works as adjective and adverb.
items.exampleCN: enough 兼作形容词和副词。

items.meaningCN: 一组读音不同的拼写组合
items.example: The -ough in enough sounds like uff.
items.exampleCN: enough 中的 -ough 读作 uff。
enough said 用来结束讨论。
fair enough 表示接受对方的解释。

definition_en: a question you ask to get information, or an official investigation
core_image: 一张写着问题的小纸条被递进窗口，里面的人开始翻资料
scene: 前台接到一通电话，对方仔细询问了房价和早餐时间。The enquiry was passed to the manager for a full answer.
sceneCN: 这里 enquiry 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：为获取信息而提出的问题）；句意：这个询问被转给经理，以便给出完整答复。

senses.title: A request for information
senses.definition: a question asked in order to get information
senses.definitionCN: 为获取信息而提出的问题
senses.example: We received an enquiry about the price of the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们收到一个询问公寓价格的电话。
senses.why: The noun names the question produced by the verb enquire.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指 enquire 这个动词所产生的「问题」。

senses.title: An official investigation
senses.definition: a formal process of finding out the facts about something
senses.definitionCN: 查明某事物事实的正式程序
senses.example: A public enquiry was opened into the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 针对这起事故启动了公开调查。
senses.why: A sustained set of questions becomes an official inquiry with its own procedure.
senses.whyCN: 持续的一连串问题会变成具有自身程序的正式调查。

senses.title: The act of asking
senses.definition: the act of asking for information rather than the question itself
senses.definitionCN: 获取信息的提问行为，而不是问题本身
senses.example: The enquiry took several days of careful checking.
senses.exampleCN: 这次询问花了好几天仔细核查。
senses.why: Like many nouns in -y, it can name the whole activity and not only its single product.
senses.whyCN: 和许多 -y 结尾的名词一样，它可指整个活动，而不只是单个产物。

intro.en: Enquiry is enquire plus the noun ending -y, from Latin inquirere, to seek into.
intro.cn: enquiry 是 enquire 加名词词尾 -y，源自拉丁语 inquirere（深入查问）。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问。

items.en: Inquirere means to search into a matter.
items.cn: inquirere 意为深入查问一件事。

items.en: Old French enquerre supplies the en- form of the verb.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 提供动词的 en- 形式。

items.en: Middle English enqueren gives the noun enquere or enquiry.
items.cn: 中古英语 enqueren 产生名词 enquere 或 enquiry。

items.en: Enquiry is used for both polite questions and formal investigations.
items.cn: enquiry 既用于礼貌询问，也用于正式调查。

items.en: British English often keeps enquiry, while American English prefers inquiry.
items.cn: 英式英语常保留 enquiry，美式英语更常用 inquiry。

note.en: Enquiry is the noun of enquire, and it sits beside inquiry, question, and investigation.
note.cn: enquiry 是 enquire 的名词，与 inquiry、question、investigation 相邻。

entries.definition: a question or investigation, Latin-style spelling
a sentence that asks for information

normalIntro.en: Enquiry is enquire plus -y, so the noun is the question or investigation that the verb produces.
normalIntro.cn: enquiry 是 enquire 加 -y，名词指动词所产生的询问或调查。

normal.en: Enquire plus -y: the thing you get when you enquire.
normal.cn: enquire 加 -y：询问之后得到的东西。

normal.en: Make an enquiry is the standard phrase for asking formally.
normal.cn: make an enquiry 是正式询问的标准搭配。

normal.en: An official enquiry is a large, structured version of a question.
normal.cn: official enquiry 是问题的「大型结构化版本」。

normal.en: Answer an enquiry is what a desk or office does.
normal.cn: answer an enquiry 是前台或办公室的常见动作。

normal.en: Compare enquiry and inquiry: same meaning, different spelling traditions.
normal.cn: 对比 enquiry 与 inquiry：意义相同，拼写传统不同。

abstract.en: Picture a note with three questions pushed across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写着三个问题的纸条被推过柜台。

abstract.en: Imagine a file labelled with a case number and filled with interviews.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标着案号、装满访谈记录的档案。

abstract.en: Think of a phone ringing at an information desk.
abstract.cn: 想象问询台的电话响起。

examples.en: She made an enquiry about the job online.
examples.cn: 她在网上询问了这份工作的情况。

examples.en: The council ordered an enquiry into the fire.
examples.cn: 议会下令调查这场火灾。

examples.en: All enquiries should be sent to the address below.
examples.cn: 所有询问请寄往下述地址。

dict_mnemonic.text: enquire（询问）+ -y（名词词尾）＝询问或调查；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: enquire（询问，源自拉丁语 inquirere「深入查问」）+ 名词词尾 -y，指提出的问题、询问行为或正式调查。

sensesIntro.en: A single question comes first, then a formal investigation, then the whole activity of asking.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是一个具体问题，再是正式调查，最后是整个询问活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question handed over and followed until it is answered.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个问题被递出去，并一路追到有答案。

branches.en: A request for information is the basic noun sense.
branches.cn: 获取信息的请求，是基本名词义项。

branches.en: A sustained and official set of questions becomes an investigation.
branches.cn: 持续而正式的一连串问题成为调查。

branches.en: The noun can also name the activity of asking as a whole.
branches.cn: 这个名词也可指整个询问活动。

branches.en: One question and the whole process of asking share the same name.
branches.cn: 单个问题与整个询问过程共享同一名称。

branches.en: A simple enquiry can grow into a public investigation.
branches.cn: 简单询问可以发展为公开调查。

intro.en: Enquiry is a French-shaped noun built on the Latin seeking root with the English ending -y.
intro.cn: enquiry 是法语形态的名词，建立在拉丁「寻求」词根上，并加英语词尾 -y。

latinIntro.en: The Latin inquirere means to seek into, from in- and quaerere, to seek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inquirere 意为深入查问，由 in- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 enquiry 开头。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of enquiry.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 enquiry 的词根。

items.example: Inquirere is the Latin source of enquiry.
items.exampleCN: inquirere 是 enquiry 的拉丁来源。

items.example: Enquire is the base of enquiry.
items.exampleCN: enquire 是 enquiry 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

items.exampleCN: enquiry 由 enquire 与 -y 合成。
enquiries 把 enquiry 变为 -ies 复数。
enquirer 共享 enquire 词干。

definition_en: to make certain that something happens or is true
core_image: 用手把门闩牢牢扣上，让事情没有出岔子的余地
scene: 出发前她把清单又核对了一遍，确认每件行李都上了车。She checked the list again to ensure that every bag was on the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 ensure 是「确保」（第 1 个义项：使某事必然发生）；句意：她又核对了一遍清单，以确保每件行李都上了车。

senses.title: To make certain an outcome
senses.definition: to take action so that something certainly happens
senses.definitionCN: 采取行动，使某事确定发生
senses.example: Please ensure that the door is locked before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 离开前请确保门已锁好。
senses.why: The word is built on sure, so the verb literally means to make an outcome sure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 sure 之上，因此动词字面上就是「使结果确定」。

senses.title: To protect or guarantee
senses.definition: to make a person or right safe from harm or unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某项权利免受伤害或不公平对待
senses.example: The new rules ensure fair treatment for all workers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定保障所有工人得到公平对待。
senses.why: Protecting people is the same certainty applied to their safety and rights.
senses.whyCN: 保护人，就是把同样的「确定」用于他们的安全与权利。

senses.title: To secure a result in advance
senses.definition: to arrange conditions so that a desired result can be secured
senses.definitionCN: 事先安排好条件，使期望的结果有把握到来
senses.example: Hard work does not ensure success, but it improves the chances.
senses.exampleCN: 努力不能确保成功，但能提高成功的可能。
senses.why: Here the word points to securing the way things turn out, not to a legal promise.
senses.whyCN: 这里指把事情的走向「锁定」，而不是法律意义上的承诺。

intro.en: Ensure comes from Anglo-Norman enseurer, from Old French asseürer, to assure, built on Latin securus, free from care.
intro.cn: ensure 来自盎格鲁-诺曼语 enseurer，源于古法语 asseürer（使确信），建立在拉丁语 securus（无忧的）之上。

items.en: Securus means free from care, from se-, apart, and cura, care.
items.cn: securus 意为无忧的，由 se-（脱离）与 cura（忧虑）构成。

items.en: Assecurare means to make safe or free from worry.
items.cn: assecurare 意为使安全、使无忧。

items.en: Asseürer carries the meaning to assure or make certain.
items.cn: asseürer 意为使确信、使有保证。

items.en: Enseurer develops the en- form used in English law and trade.
items.cn: enseurer 发展出英语法律与商业中使用的 en- 形式。

items.en: Middle English ensuren means to make safe or certain.
items.cn: 中古英语 ensuren 意为使安全或使确定。

items.en: Modern English uses ensure mainly for making an outcome certain.
items.cn: 现代英语中，ensure 主要用于表示「使结果确定」。

note.en: Ensure belongs to the sure family, and it sits near verbs for guaranteeing and securing.
note.cn: ensure 属于「确定」词族，与表示保证和确保的动词相邻。

entries.definition: to protect against loss with an insurance policy
to tell someone confidently that something is true
to promise that something will certainly happen
to make something safe or certain
to make a fact or arrangement certain

normalIntro.en: Ensure contains sure: the whole point of the verb is to make an outcome sure.
normalIntro.cn: ensure 含有 sure：这个动词的全部要点就是让结果「确定」。

normal.en: En- turns the adjective sure into a verb meaning make sure.
normal.cn: 前缀 en- 把形容词 sure 变成动词，意为「使确定」。

normal.en: Ensure that is the most common pattern, and it is followed by a full clause.
normal.cn: ensure that 是最常见的搭配，后面接完整从句。

normal.en: Keep ensure and insure apart: one makes certain, the other buys insurance.
normal.cn: 把 ensure 与 insure 分开：一个表示使确定，另一个表示买保险。

normal.en: Compare assure: assure works on people, while ensure works on outcomes.
normal.cn: 对比 assure：assure 的对象是人，ensure 的对象是结果。

normal.en: In formal writing, ensure often replaces make sure.
normal.cn: 在正式写作中，ensure 常用来替代 make sure。

abstract.en: Picture a latch clicked shut, so the door cannot swing open in the night.
abstract.cn: 想象门闩咔嗒扣上，夜里门再也吹不开。

abstract.en: Imagine checking every seat belt before the bus leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象大巴出发前逐条检查安全带。

abstract.en: Think of a knot pulled tight so the load cannot slip.
abstract.cn: 想象绳结被拉紧，货物不会滑脱。

examples.en: The nurse ensured that the patient was comfortable.
examples.cn: 护士确保病人躺得舒服。

examples.en: Regular checks ensure the machines run safely.
examples.cn: 定期检查确保机器安全运转。

examples.en: To ensure a seat, book your ticket early.
examples.cn: 想确保有座位，就早点订票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因 sure」——因为确定，所以 ensure 就是确保；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 securus（无忧的）→ 俗拉丁语 assecurare（使安全）→ 古法语 asseürer → 盎格鲁-诺曼语 enseurer → 中古英语 ensuren → 现代英语 ensure，核心义「使确定无疑」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from freedom from care to the act of making an outcome certain, then to legal and practical guarantees.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「无忧」出发，转到「使结果确定」的动作，再延伸到法律与实际层面的保障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a latch fastened so that the outcome cannot slip away.
core.cn: 核心意象：门闩扣紧，结果无法溜走。

branches.en: Making an outcome certain is the everyday core sense.
branches.cn: 使结果确定，是日常的核心义项。

branches.en: Protecting people or rights extends the same certainty into safety.
branches.cn: 保护人或权利，把同样的确定延伸到安全。

branches.en: Securing a result means arranging the conditions in advance.
branches.cn: 确保得到结果，就是事先安排条件。

branches.en: Certainty and safety are two sides of the same promise.
branches.cn: 确定与安全是同一个承诺的两面。

branches.en: Protection and advance planning often appear together in rules.
branches.cn: 保护与事前规划常一起出现在规则里。

intro.en: Ensure is a French-shaped verb with a Latin core, and its small family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: ensure 是法语形态的动词，核心来自拉丁语，其小词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura means care, securus means free from care, and assecurare means to make safe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 表示忧虑，securus 表示无忧，assecurare 表示使安全。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 ensure 与 enlarge 开头。

items.example: Securus is the deep root behind ensure.
items.exampleCN: securus 是 ensure 背后的深层词根。

items.example: Se- in securus means apart from care.
items.exampleCN: securus 中的 se- 意为脱离忧虑。

items.example: Cura supplies the idea of care.
items.exampleCN: cura 提供「关心、忧虑」的意思。
assecurare 把两部分连接起来。

items.example: Asseürer carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: asseürer 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Enseurer gives English its en- form.
items.exampleCN: enseurer 为英语提供 en- 形式。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词词尾

items.example: Ensurance is now archaic or rare.
items.exampleCN: ensurance 现在已古旧或罕见。

definition_en: to go or come into a place, group, activity, or system
core_image: 推开一扇门，脚跨过门槛，从外面走到里面
scene: 电梯门一开，他侧身让老人先走进去。He stepped aside and let the old man enter the lift first.
sceneCN: 这里 enter 是「进入」（第 1 个义项：从外面走到里面）；句意：他侧身让老人先走进电梯。

senses.title: To go into a place
senses.definition: to move from outside into a room, building, or area
senses.definitionCN: 从外面移动到房间、建筑或区域内部
senses.example: She entered the hall without making a sound.
senses.exampleCN: 她悄无声息地走进了大厅。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to go inside, so the physical movement through a doorway is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「走到里面」，所以穿过门口的身体移动是核心义项。

senses.title: To join an activity or group
senses.definition: to become involved in a competition, course, organization, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 参与比赛、课程、组织或协议
senses.example: He entered the competition for the first time this year.
senses.exampleCN: 他今年第一次参加这项比赛。
senses.why: Joining a group is pictured as crossing into a shared space.
senses.whyCN: 加入一个群体，被想象成走进一个共同的空间。

senses.title: To type information in
senses.definition: to put information into a computer, form, or record
senses.definitionCN: 把信息写入电脑、表格或记录
senses.example: Enter your password and press return.
senses.exampleCN: 输入密码，然后按回车键。
senses.why: A system is treated as a place, and data crosses its boundary when it is entered.
senses.whyCN: 系统被看作一个场所，数据被输入时就越过了它的边界。

intro.en: Enter comes from Latin intrare, to go in, from intra, within, through Old French entrer.
intro.cn: enter 来自拉丁语 intrare（进入），源于 intra（在内），经古法语 entrer 进入英语。

items.en: Intra means within or inside.
items.cn: intra 意为在内、在内部。

items.en: Intrare means to go in or enter.
items.cn: intrare 意为走进、进入。

items.en: Entrer carries the verb into French with the same doorway image.
items.cn: entrer 把这个动词带入法语，保留同样的门口画面。

items.en: The verb enters English law for entering land or a house.
items.cn: 这个动词进入英语法律，用于进入土地或房屋。

items.en: Middle English entren extends to records and lists.
items.cn: 中古英语 entren 扩展到记录与名单。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of entering data into a system.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「把数据输入系统」的义项。

note.en: Enter is a doorway verb, and it sits near derived nouns for going in and near verbs for joining.
note.cn: enter 是一个「门口」动词，与表示进入的派生名词及表示加入的动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of going in or an item in a list
a door or the act of entering
a person who takes part in something
to move into a room from outside
to become a member of a group

normalIntro.en: Enter begins with en-, the same in-prefix found in include, so the word itself says go in.
normalIntro.cn: enter 以 en- 开头，与 include 中表示「内」的前缀相同，所以这个词本身就说「走进去」。

normal.en: En- means in, and the rest of the word carries the movement into a space.
normal.cn: en- 表示内，其余部分承载走进空间的动作。

normal.en: Enter a room is physical, while enter a competition is social.
normal.cn: enter a room 是身体动作，enter a competition 是社会行为。

normal.en: Enter data shows the word moving from doors to keyboards.
normal.cn: enter data 表明这个词从门口走到了键盘。

normal.en: The noun entrance keeps the same idea of crossing a threshold.
normal.cn: 名词 entrance 保留「跨过门槛」的同一意象。

normal.en: Compare enter and entry: the verb acts, the noun names the act or the item.
normal.cn: 对比 enter 与 entry：动词表示动作，名词表示行为或条目。

abstract.en: Picture a foot lifting over a wooden threshold.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚抬起，跨过木门槛。

abstract.en: Imagine a keypad blinking before the door unlocks.
abstract.cn: 想象键盘闪了一下，门随即打开。

abstract.en: Think of a name being written on a list at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象名字在门口被写进一份名单。

examples.en: She entered the hall quietly and sat at the back.
examples.cn: 她安静地走进大厅，坐在后排。

examples.en: He entered the competition for the first time this year.
examples.cn: 他今年第一次参加这项比赛。

examples.en: Enter your password and press return to continue.
examples.cn: 输入密码并按回车键继续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摁门」——伸手摁开门，人就进去了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intra（在内）→ 拉丁语 intrare（进入）→ 古法语 entrer → 中古英语 entren → 现代英语 enter。

sensesIntro.en: Enter starts as a physical movement through a doorway and extends to joining groups and feeding data into systems.
sensesIntro.cn: enter 从穿过门口的身体动作开始，扩展到加入群体以及把数据送入系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot crossing a threshold from outside to inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚跨过门槛，从外到内。

branches.en: Physical movement into a place is the core sense.
branches.cn: 身体进入某地，是核心义项。

branches.en: Joining a group treats membership as a space to enter.
branches.cn: 加入群体，把成员身份当作可进入的空间。

branches.en: Typing data treats a system as a place with a boundary.
branches.cn: 输入数据，把系统看作有边界的场所。

branches.en: Both a room and a group can be entered.
branches.cn: 房间与群体都可以「进入」。

branches.en: A record and a group both keep the names of those inside.
branches.cn: 记录与群体都保存着「在里面」者的名字。

intro.en: Enter is a Latin verb reshaped by French, and its family grows with English noun endings.
intro.cn: enter 是经法语改造的拉丁动词，其词族由英语名词词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin intra means within, and intrare means to go inside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intra 表示在内，intrare 表示走进。

items.example: Intra is the old form behind enter.
items.exampleCN: intra 是 enter 背后的古老形式。

items.example: Intrare is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: intrare 是直接的拉丁语来源。
entrer 使拉丁语形态变得柔和。

items.example: Enter is the modern English form.

items.meaning: a way in or the act of entering

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或场所的词尾

items.meaning: the act of entering or an item
items.example: Entry is a shorter related noun.
items.exampleCN: entry 是更短的相关名词。

definition_en: a business or bold project, or the initiative needed to undertake one
core_image: 一队人带着工具走出城门，去把一桩有风险的大事做成
scene: 小镇上那家做太阳能板的企业去年雇了三十名工人。The enterprise that makes solar panels in the town hired thirty workers last year.
sceneCN: 这里 enterprise 是「企业」（第 1 个义项：从事经营活动的组织）；句意：镇上那家生产太阳能板的企业去年雇了三十名工人。

derivatives.zh: 有进取心的；有事业心的

senses.title: A business organization
senses.definition: a company or business, especially a commercial one
senses.definitionCN: 公司或商业组织，尤指营利性的
senses.example: The family runs a small printing enterprise.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人经营着一家小型印刷企业。
senses.why: An enterprise is first something undertaken, and a business is the most common thing undertaken in modern life.
senses.whyCN: enterprise 本指「所承担之事」，而现代生活中最常见的承担之事就是经营。

senses.title: A bold or difficult project
senses.definition: an ambitious project that involves effort and risk
senses.definitionCN: 需要付出努力并承担风险的宏大计划
senses.example: Building the bridge was a bold enterprise.
senses.exampleCN: 修建这座桥是一项大胆的事业。
senses.why: The original French noun names something undertaken, so any large risky task fits.
senses.whyCN: 法语原名词指「着手去做的事」，因此任何宏大而冒险的任务都符合。

senses.title: Initiative and boldness
senses.definition: the quality of being willing to start new and difficult things
senses.definitionCN: 愿意开创全新而困难之事的品质
senses.example: She showed great enterprise in opening the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她开这家店，表现出很强的进取心。
senses.why: The willingness to undertake is abstracted into a personal quality.
senses.whyCN: 「敢于承担」被抽象为一种个人品质。

intro.en: Enterprise comes from Old French entreprise, something undertaken, from entreprendre, to take in hand, built on Latin inter and prehendere.
intro.cn: enterprise 来自古法语 entreprise（所承担之事），源于 entreprendre（着手去做），由拉丁语 inter 与 prehendere 构成。

items.en: Inter means between or among.
items.cn: inter 意为在……之间。

items.en: Prehendere means to seize or take hold of.
items.cn: prehendere 意为抓住、握住。

items.en: Entreprendre means to undertake or take in hand.
items.cn: entreprendre 意为着手、承担。

items.en: Entreprise names the thing undertaken.
items.cn: entreprise 指所承担的事情。

items.en: Middle English enterprise covers bold deeds as well as business.
items.cn: 中古英语 enterprise 既指大胆行动，也指商业经营。

items.en: Modern English separates the business, project, and initiative senses.
items.cn: 现代英语分化出企业、事业与进取心三个义项。

note.en: Enterprise is an undertaking noun, and it sits near its own derivatives and near words for business and ventures.
note.cn: enterprise 是一个「承担之事」名词，与自身派生词以及表示商业和冒险事业的词相邻。

entries.definition: willing to start new and bold things
a person who starts a business
an organization that sells goods or services

normalIntro.en: Enterprise contains prise, from French prendre, to take: it is the taking up of a task.
normalIntro.cn: enterprise 含有 prise，来自法语 prendre（拿取）：它就是「把事情接过来做」。

normal.en: Entre- means between, and prendre means take: taking something in hand.
normal.cn: entre- 表示之间，prendre 表示拿取：把事情接到手里。

normal.en: A business enterprise is an undertaking that must pay its way.
normal.cn: 商业企业是一项必须自己养活自己的事业。

normal.en: Spirit of enterprise names the courage to start something risky.
normal.cn: spirit of enterprise 指敢于开创冒险之事的勇气。

normal.en: Entrepreneur is the person, while enterprise is the thing or the quality.
normal.cn: entrepreneur 是人，enterprise 是事情或品质。

normal.en: Compare venture: both involve risk, but enterprise also means a company.
normal.cn: 对比 venture：两者都含风险，但 enterprise 还可指公司。

abstract.en: Picture a group setting out at dawn with tools and a map.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人带着工具和地图，在黎明出发。

abstract.en: Imagine a merchant signing a contract on a busy quay.
abstract.cn: 想象一位商人在繁忙的码头上签下合同。

abstract.en: Think of a seed pushed into hard ground before any shoot appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子被按进硬土，嫩芽尚未出现。

examples.en: The family runs a small printing enterprise.
examples.cn: 这家人经营着一家小型印刷企业。

examples.en: Building the bridge was a bold enterprise.
examples.cn: 修建这座桥是一项大胆的事业。

examples.en: She showed great enterprise in opening the shop.
examples.cn: 她开这家店，表现出很强的进取心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enter prize」——敢进场去拿奖，就是有进取心的事业；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（之间）＋ prehendere（抓取）→ 古法语 entreprendre（着手做）→ entreprise（所承担之事）→ 中古英语 enterprise → 现代英语 enterprise。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins as something taken in hand, then narrows to a business, widens to any bold project, and finally names the courage behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词最初指「接到手里的事」，随后收窄为商业企业，又扩展为任何大胆事业，最后指背后的勇气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group setting out to take a risky task in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人出发，把有风险的任务接到手里。

branches.en: A business is the most concrete modern undertaking.
branches.cn: 企业是现代社会最具体的「承担之事」。

branches.en: A bold project keeps the original sense of something undertaken.
branches.cn: 大胆事业保留「所承担之事」的原义。

branches.en: Initiative is the personal quality that starts undertakings.
branches.cn: 进取心是开创事业所需的个人品质。

branches.en: A company and a large project both require planning and risk.
branches.cn: 公司与大型项目都需要规划与冒险。

branches.en: Bold projects exist because someone supplies the initiative.
branches.cn: 大胆事业之所以存在，是因为有人提供进取心。

intro.en: Enterprise is a French noun built from entre and prendre, with English endings forming its modern family.
intro.cn: enterprise 是由 entre 与 prendre 构成的法语名词，现代词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between, and prehendere means to seize; French entreprendre joins them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 表示之间，prehendere 表示抓取；法语 entreprendre 把两者结合。

items.exampleCN: entre- 出现在 entreprendre 与 enterprise 开头。

items.example: Inter is the Latin source of entre-.
items.exampleCN: inter 是 entre- 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Prehendere is the deep root of prendre.
items.exampleCN: prehendere 是 prendre 的深层词根。

items.example: Entreprendre means to take something in hand.
items.exampleCN: entreprendre 意为把事情接到手里。

items.example: Entreprise is the direct source of enterprise.
items.exampleCN: entreprise 是 enterprise 的直接来源。
enterprise 保留「承担之事」的含义。

items.example: Enterprising describes a person or plan.
Entrepreneur names the person who undertakes.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或品质的词尾

definition_en: shows, activities, or hospitality that amuse people or look after guests
core_image: 灯光、音乐与笑声组成的一整晚，还有摆满食物的餐桌
scene: 演出开始前，剧场经理说今晚的娱乐节目会持续到午夜。Before the show began, the theatre manager said the evening's entertainment would last until midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 entertainment 是「娱乐节目」（第 1 个义项：使人开心的演出或活动）；句意：演出开始前，剧场经理说今晚的娱乐节目会持续到午夜。

senses.title: Shows and activities that amuse
senses.definition: films, music, games, or other things that give people pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 电影、音乐、游戏等给人快乐的事物
senses.example: The hotel offers live entertainment every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店每晚都有现场娱乐表演。
senses.why: The noun names the things produced when people are entertained.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指人们被娱乐时所产生的事物。

senses.title: The act of entertaining guests
senses.definition: the activity of welcoming and looking after guests
senses.definitionCN: 迎接并照顾客人的活动
senses.example: Their hospitality was more than mere entertainment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的好客不只是表面的招待。
senses.why: The old hospitality sense of the verb survives in the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词古老的待客义项在名词中保留下来。

senses.title: A performance or event
senses.definition: a particular show or event that people watch for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 人们为消遣而观看的某场演出或活动
senses.example: The concert was good entertainment for the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 这场音乐会对全家来说都是很好的消遣。
senses.why: One instance of amusing activity is counted as a piece of entertainment.
senses.whyCN: 一次具体的娱乐活动，就算作一件娱乐节目。

intro.en: Entertainment is entertain plus the noun ending -ment; the verb comes from Old French entretenir, to hold together.
intro.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 加名词词尾 -ment；动词来自古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）。

items.en: Tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: Entretenir means to hold together and maintain.
items.cn: entretenir 意为使相聚、维持。

items.en: Middle English entretinen gives the base verb.
items.cn: 中古英语 entretinen 提供基础动词。

items.en: The noun entertainment appears for hospitality and amusement.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，名词 entertainment 出现，表示招待与娱乐。

items.en: Public shows and the entertainment industry expand the word.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，公共演出与娱乐业扩展了这个词的用法。

items.en: Modern English uses entertainment for both shows and hospitality.
items.cn: 现代英语中，entertainment 既指节目，也指待客。

note.en: Entertainment is the -ment noun of entertain, and it sits near its family and near words for amusement and shows.
note.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 的 -ment 名词，与自身词族以及表示娱乐和演出的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who amuses an audience
the feeling of finding something funny or enjoyable
activity done for pleasure when not working

normalIntro.en: Entertainment is entertain plus -ment, so it names the pleasure and the shows that result from entertaining.
normalIntro.cn: entertainment 是 entertain 加 -ment，指招待与娱乐所带来的快乐和节目。

normal.en: The ending -ment turns the verb into the activity or its result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 把动词变成活动或活动的结果。

normal.en: The entertainment industry is built on holding attention.
normal.cn: 娱乐业建立在「留住注意力」之上。

normal.en: Live entertainment means performers in front of a real audience.
normal.cn: live entertainment 指真人在观众面前表演。

normal.en: For entertainment is the phrase that names the purpose.
normal.cn: for entertainment 是说明目的的常用短语。

normal.en: Compare amusement: amusement is often the feeling, while entertainment is often the show.
normal.cn: 对比 amusement：amusement 常指感受，entertainment 常指节目。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre before the curtain rises, seats filling with chatter.
abstract.cn: 想象大幕拉开前的剧场，座位间满是交谈声。

abstract.en: Imagine a table cleared for cards and laughter after dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象晚饭后桌子被清出来打牌，笑声不断。

abstract.en: Think of a band tuning up while the lights dim.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光变暗，乐队正在调音。

examples.en: The hotel offers live entertainment every evening.
examples.cn: 这家酒店每晚都有现场娱乐表演。

examples.en: Their hospitality was more than mere entertainment.
examples.cn: 他们的好客不只是表面的招待。

examples.en: The concert was good entertainment for the whole family.
examples.cn: 这场音乐会对全家来说都是很好的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「entertain + ment」——把人留住、让人开心的那件事，就是娱乐；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ 古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持）→ 中古英语 entretinen → entertain（招待、娱乐）＋ -ment → entertainment（娱乐；招待）。

sensesIntro.en: The noun covers the feeling and activity of being amused, the old duty of looking after guests, and the concrete shows that produce pleasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词涵盖被娱乐的感受与活动、古老的待客职责，以及产生快乐的具体节目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an evening of lights, music, and laughter shared with others.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯光、音乐与笑声共享的一晚。

branches.en: Shows and games are the most visible form of entertainment.
branches.cn: 演出与游戏是最显眼的娱乐形式。

branches.en: Hospitality is entertainment in its oldest social form.
branches.cn: 待客是娱乐最古老的社交形式。

branches.en: A single performance is counted as one entertainment.
branches.cn: 一场演出可算作一项娱乐活动。

branches.en: The industry produces events, and each event is an entertainment.
branches.cn: 娱乐业生产活动，每场活动就是一项娱乐。

branches.en: A host's evening and a public show both aim at pleasure.
branches.cn: 主人的晚宴与公开演出都以快乐为目标。

intro.en: Entertainment is an English -ment noun built on the French-shaped verb entertain.
intro.cn: entertainment 是建立在法语形态动词 entertain 上的英语 -ment 名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is tenere, to hold; French entretenir keeps people together, and English adds -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 tenere（握住）；法语 entretenir 使人相聚，英语再加 -ment。

items.exampleCN: entre- 出现在 entretenir 开头。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

items.example: Entertainment names the activity and its result.
